findings.summary: A 2D geometric model represents objects as planar figures on a Euclidean or Cartesian plane, sufficient for flat entities like sheet metal parts or circular storm models viewed from above. It serves as a foundational tool in 2D computer graphics and technical diagrams, often functioning as a component within larger 3D constructions, such as automobile decals. Modern architecture employs digital rendering techniques to simulate three-dimensional perception from these two-dimensional representations.

mechanisms.title: Planar Representation
mechanisms.explanation: Objects are encoded as two-dimensional figures, allowing adequate description of flat physical entities and serving as building blocks for complex 3D structures.

mechanisms.title: Integration in Graphics and Rendering
mechanisms.explanation: These models are essential for 2D graphics and are frequently used as components in 3D models; modern architecture uses digital rendering to convey 3D perception from 2D geometric data.
